extracted.intended_audience: museum professionals, grant program staff, policymakers, and program evaluators
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation metrics and findings for the Institute of Museum and Library Services' Museums for America (MFA) grant program, describing measures of partnership effects, institutional and staff capacity, audience and programming outcomes, collections stewardship, and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: At least one partnership effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator whether a project had at least one partnership-related effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-8 finding: 70% of projects reported at least one partnership effect (sample FY2004–FY2008, n=325).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthened ongoing partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the grant strengthened existing/ongoing partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-8: 62% overall; higher for Programming and Technology projects; small museums reported 78% for strengthening ongoing partnerships. Interviews stress mutual goals and mutual benefits as keys to sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developed new partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the grant led to formation of new partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-8: 53% overall; partnerships sometimes formed for specific purposes (e.g., after-school programs) and leveraged resources and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improved skills in building partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether staff reported improved partnership-building skills as a result of the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-8: 44% overall; small museums showed the greatest improvement (58%). Qualitative comments note learning to develop systems for sustaining relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased ability to attract more partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the grant increased the institution’s ability to attract additional partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-8: 36% overall; rises with grant size (small awards 36%, medium 42%, large 48%). Partnerships also associated with increased public awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developed new types of partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the grant enabled formation of new kinds of partnerships not previously pursued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-8: 36% overall; frequency increases with award size (small 25%, medium 34%, large 41%). Examples include virtual park exhibits and internship collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships' contribution to longer-term effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether working with partners resulted in a greater number of longer-term effects across areas like audience and organizational capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis: 41% of respondents with partnerships reported effects in 3–6 areas compared with 19% without partnerships. Qualitative examples highlight sustained partnerships and new capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships increased public awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether partnerships helped raise the museum’s public profile or visibility as a community learning center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-quarters of surveyed museums that worked with partners reported increased public awareness; partnerships are linked to reputational gains especially for small museums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships increased access to resources and personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether partnerships provided access to resources, volunteers, or paid staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: About half of surveyed museums reported partnerships increased access to resources; one-third reported access to new paid staff or volunteers. Some partners brought in new members.

rubrics_metrics.name: At least one organizational capacity effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator whether a project produced at least one positive effect on organizational capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-9: 98% of respondents indicated at least one organizational capacity effect (n=464).

rubrics_metrics.name: Helped institution fulfill its mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the grant helped the museum better fulfill its mission or meet benchmarks tied to its mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-9: 81% overall; higher (86%) for largest award category versus 72% for smallest. Qualitative data show mission refinement and incorporation into strategic plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased ability to attract outside funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the grant improved the museum’s capacity to secure additional funding from IMLS or other sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-9: 67% reported improved ability to attract outside funding. Examples include leveraging MFA projects to access large grants or meeting prerequisites for challenge grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improved staff cohesion and commitment to mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the grant improved staff cohesion and alignment with the museum’s mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-9: 45% reported improved staff cohesion and commitment. Some projects created new staff roles or hiring criteria aligned with initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greater board involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether board engagement with the museum increased as a result of the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-9: 19% reported greater board involvement as an effect of the MFA grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greater alignment of staff responsibilities with mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether staff roles and responsibilities became more aligned with the museum’s mission following the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-9: 31% reported greater alignment. Some institutions changed hiring criteria or created positions to align capabilities with initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced staff capacity in reaching new or larger audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether staff gained skills or capacity to reach broader or new audience segments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-10: 72% reported enhanced capacity. Qualitative examples include learning strategies for different ages, learning styles, and accessibility needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced staff capacity in program development
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether staff increased their capability to design and deliver programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-10: 62% reported increased capacity in program development; many projects led to new programming beyond initial MFA activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced staff capacity in forming external partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether staff improved their ability to form and manage partnerships with external organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-10: 52% reported enhanced partnership-forming capacity; partnerships often leveraged resources and expanded audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced staff capacity in working internally across departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether staff improved cross-departmental collaboration within the museum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-10: 50% overall; effect increased with museum size (large 60%, medium 47%, small 35%). Some projects required all departments to collaborate on equal footing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced staff capacity in creating new kinds of exhibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether staff gained the ability to design or produce new exhibition types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-10: 46% reported increased capacity to create new exhibitions, e.g., incorporating kinesthetic elements or interactive storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced staff capacity in using outcomes-based evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether staff improved use of outcomes-based planning and evaluation methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit IV-10: 41% reported improvement. Interviewees praised IMLS materials on logic models and outcomes-based planning; many learned online survey tools and summative evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience reach — attracted new audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the project attracted new audiences to the museum (new demographics or groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nearly three-quarters of sampled museums that reached out to public audiences reported reaching new audiences. Partnerships and tailored local designs helped attract diverse groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience commitment — increased audience commitment to the institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether audience members showed greater commitment (e.g., volunteerism, repeat visits) after the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Almost two-thirds reported gains in audience commitment. Examples include higher volunteer rates and sustained school group demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased audience access
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the project improved physical, digital, or programmatic access for audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nearly half reported increased audience access via interactive websites, mobile programming, expanded hours, clearer signage, better ADA accessibility, resource sharing, and longer-term commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience retention/sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether museums were successful in retaining audiences reached during the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nearly all institutions that conducted projects for external audiences indicated some success in retaining those audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming sustained or continued after grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether programming initiated or underwritten by the MFA grant was sustained post-grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More than two-thirds reported programming sustained or continued; many considered their continuation 'very successful.' Projects were often written into budgets or funded by additional grants/partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program expansion — capacity to conduct related programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the project increased capacity to undertake additional related programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A majority (90–98% in some categories) reported greater capacity to conduct related programming. Over half of programming/exhibition projects generated additional programming beyond proposed activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to mission refinement or change
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the grant contributed to strengthening, refining, or changing institutional mission and strategic plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitative examples: mission re-visioning at Genesee Country Village; integration of project outcomes into strategic plans (e.g., Chicago Botanic Garden). All Organizational Development projects reported longer-term effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting mission-related benchmarks/strategic goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the project helped museums meet key benchmarks and align work with mission/strategic plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four-fifths of responding museums reported meeting benchmarks related to mission and strategic plans; projects often used outcomes-based planning to stay focused on desired outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collections stewardship — digitization and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the project advanced collections stewardship through digitization, inventories, management plans, or increased access to collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 34% of surveyed museums undertook digitization/collections activities; among those digitizing, nearly 25% digitized at least half of collections and over 80% created new digital content. Activities also included oral histories and archival research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unifying collections and cross-site integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the project unified collections within an institution or across multiple sites for better stewardship and access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include master interpretive plans that integrated disparate holdings; unification often paved the way for additional funding and strategic clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of new collections materials or research-based reinterpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the project produced new collection materials (e.g., oral histories) or research that reinterprets collections for exhibits/programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case examples: Akwesasne Cultural Center interviews with basket-makers; USS Constitution Museum research on crew members used to ground exhibits and programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of logic models and outcomes-based planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether grantees used logic models and outcomes-based planning to define and measure desired outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviewees reported IMLS materials and logic models helped stay focused on desired outcomes; many reported greater sophistication in summative evaluation and survey tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation capacity — summative evaluation skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the project increased grantees’ ability to design and use summative evaluations and online survey tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many reported improved use of online surveys and tailoring questionnaires; increased ability to use outcomes-based evaluation as a learning tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation/community profile effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the MFA grant enhanced the museum’s public image, visibility, or role as a center of community learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nearly nine in ten responding museums reported at least one positive effect on community profile; nearly two-thirds reported greater visibility as community learning centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant size correlation with effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the size of the MFA award is associated with broader organizational or partnership effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger awards correlated with broader organizational capacity effects (e.g., highest percentage reporting help in fulfilling mission). Larger awards were associated with higher rates of attracting partners and developing new partnership types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum size differences in effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether museum size (small/medium/large) affects the magnitude or type of grant effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small museums often reported larger percentage gains in partnership skill-building and benefit from prestige; large museums reported greater internal cross-department collaboration gains. Award effects varied by museum size on some measures but not others (e.g., little variation in strengthening ongoing partnerships by grant size).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process as a capacity-building tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the application and review process itself helps museums clarify strategic goals and secure other funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 78% of sampled applicants reported the application process helped clarify strategic goals. However, small museums noted application burden; award rates improve with repeat applications (average funding after 1.5 attempts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability post-grant (financial and institutional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether projects were sustained financially and institutionally after the grant ended (written into budgets, funded by other grants, or supported by partners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many projects were sustained via operating budgets, additional IMLS or external grants, corporate sponsors, or partner support; three out of five respondents described sustaining efforts as 'very successful.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth/quality of partnership relationships (mutual goals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether partnerships are built on mutual goals and complementary activities that yield mutual benefits and sustainability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interview evidence (Pratt Museum, others) emphasizes that mutual goals and integral activities are key to sustainability and mutual benefit; grants helped clarify 'how and why to partner.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic innovation and institutional transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the grant led to programmatic innovations or transformations in how the institution operates (new content knowledge, pedagogical approaches, roles, or mission shifts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include new interactivity and storytelling techniques, new staff roles, mission reorientation toward environmental sustainability, and projects that transformed institutional operations or public offerings.
